newsitem.title: USA: White House tries to rally support for Herman.
newsitem.headline: White House tries to rally support for Herman.

text.p: The White House Friday tried to rally support for embattled Labour Secretary nominee Alexis Herman by encouraging organisations concerned with labour, women and civil rights to speak out on her behalf.

White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles and a deputy, John Podesta, met with about 75 representatives from the groups to give them an update on Herman's situation and urge them to come to her defence.

Senate Republicans have questioned whether Herman, as director of the White House office for public liaison, violated the law when her office invited a federal banking regulator to a political coffee meeting at the White House with Clinton and bankers.

"We think the nomination is in good shape on the Hill," McCurry said. "She needs her hearing so that she can address any questions the senators have. But we're confident that she will get the hearing and be confirmed."

Bowles spoke earlier this week with the committee's chairman, Sen. James Jeffords, Vermont Republican. Jeffords said Wednesday he was not trying to delay Herman's hearing unnecessarily but did not want to schedule it until questions about her were resolved.
McCurry said the White House urged the Herman supporters to "do what we're doing, to publicly say it's time to move on and get a date, and proceed with confirmation."
